decisions.reason: Although its manual workstation format is less central than the firm's more automated Industry 4.0 push, it still extends the laser-marking portfolio and a large growing supplier would usually keep this option open unless weak demand becomes clear.

This thermal inkjet printer sits very close to the firm's core coding applications, so with a growing market and low strategic mismatch the firm is likely to continue learning from it rather than withdraw it.

The piezo inkjet printer also fits the established offer, but its somewhat more specialized positioning makes pruning modestly more plausible than for the thermal inkjet product if sales remain narrow.

As a 2024 flagship line highlighted on the home page and aligned with the firm's direction toward digitalized traceability, this product has very high option value and very little reason to be abandoned so soon.

The compact laser marking cabin builds directly on the firm's laser competence and broadens the solution set for customers, so management would typically keep it on the market while demand by application becomes clearer.
The lubricant printing system is specialized, but the award signal materially improves its perceived upside, so a resource-rich R&D-active firm would usually retain it as a promising niche option.
